fatal_errors: Replaces the target temperature-dependent deformation study of single-phase FCC solid solutions with an aging-and-precipitation study.

Assumes precipitates without evidence; the target materials were homogenized, quenched concentrated solid solutions whose strength was linked to lattice distortion and solute-mediated glide resistance.
Omits the central cryogenic inertial-dulling, MSAD-strength scaling, and high-temperature Portevin–Le Chatelier mechanisms.
Provides no supporting evidence or citations.
The falsification rule is internally inconsistent: the prediction says strength should increase with aging, but the rule treats failure of strength to decrease as falsification.
explanation: The response only aligns at the very broad level that dislocations interact with solutes. Its proposed aging intervention, precipitation mediator, 20–500 °C range, and strength–ductility outcome do not reconstruct the controlled comparison of equiatomic FCC single crystals compressed from 9 to 1373 K. It misses the composition-dependent MSAD control of extrapolated 0 K CRSS, phonon-drag-controlled inertial dulling below roughly 60–77 K, and Mn/Fe-associated Cottrell-type dynamic solute pinning and serrated flow at elevated temperature. Although aged-versus-unaged specimens form a nominal control, the measurements would not discriminate the target mechanisms, and the contradictory falsification criterion further weakens the design.
